name: v0.3.0
body:
Mini-Me Desktop for Windows — a research workbench that runs on your own machine.

**This is the first published release.** Everything before it was a draft, visible
only to people with repository access.

## What's new in 0.3.0

Fifty-six merged changes since `v0.2.3` was built on 18 August.

### AutoDiscovery

Ask for a discovery run in plain language and Allen AI's AutoDiscovery searches
hypotheses over your dataset. The whole thing is new here.

- **Nothing is charged without your press.** The budget arrives as a modal in the
  centre of the window: what it will cost in credits, what the balance is, the
  guiding intent as editable text, and the number of experiments to buy. Accept,
  change it, or walk away. The agent cannot submit a run on its own — that is
  enforced in the backend, not only in the prompt.
- **The experiment tree**, drawn from the run's own parent edges. Click a node to
  open that experiment.
- **Per experiment**: the hypothesis, the analysis and the review, rendered as
  Markdown, with the plots the run produced.
- **A ranked table**, sorted by how far each experiment moved the belief — press
  the button to reverse it. A failed or still-running experiment sorts above a
  quiet finished one, because a status matters more than a score.
- **Full screen** for the results, which are long enough to want reading room.

### Datasets and papers

- A **dataset panel** with a download button for the datasets that are open, and
  four kinds of dataset told apart rather than lumped together.
- Files you attach are **copied into the conversation folder**, so a run reads them
  from a path it can actually see.
- A **library** can now span more than one turn.

### Long jobs

- The background-jobs panel **folds and stays bounded**, so a long plan no longer
  pushes the conversation off screen.
- A run that finished while nobody was looking is **collected and announced once**,
  and the notice can be dismissed for good.
- **A desktop notification** when a long job ends and you are in another window.
  Nothing pops up while you are watching.

### Underneath

- **Contract tests** between every backend payload and the app that decodes it: a
  field the backend adds and the app ignores now fails a test instead of going
  quietly missing.
- `langgraph-api` upgraded off a version that was End of Life and said so on every
  launch.
- Charts that arrived base64-encoded are decoded rather than shown as text.
- Errors now say **what** failed rather than only that something did — three
  separate places were swallowing the one message worth reading.

## Install

1. Download the zip below and unzip it anywhere.
2. Double-click **mini-me-desktop-app.exe**.
3. Windows will say *"Windows protected your PC"* — this build is not
   code-signed. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
4. The Setup pane opens and tells you what is missing. Press the buttons.
5. Open Settings (ctrl-,) and paste a model API key.

No terminal, no GitHub account, no Python install. The backend is included.

**The first run installs WSL** if this machine has never had it. That step asks for
administrator rights and then **needs a restart** — reopen the app afterwards and the
Setup pane picks up where it left off. Nothing to type at any point.

## Updating from an earlier build

Unzip this one over the old folder, or beside it. Your conversations and files live
in **Documents\Mini-Me** and your keys in Windows Credential Manager, so neither is
touched by replacing the application folder.

An in-app update button is the next thing being built; until it exists, updating
means downloading this zip.

## Notes

- Keys go in Windows Credential Manager, never in a file.
- Files the agent creates land in **Documents\Mini-Me**, one folder per conversation.
- Commands the agent wants to run wait for your approval first.
- Long jobs show the agent's own plan, so you can see how far through it is.

## If something goes wrong

Send back **three things** and it can usually be diagnosed without a call:

1. The line under **THIS BUILD** in the About page (the ⌂ icon, top left).
2. `%TEMP%\mini-me-desktop-app.log` — what the app did.
3. `%TEMP%\mini-me-desktop-backend.log` — what the agent did.

Both logs are rewritten on each launch, so they describe the run that just failed.
Neither contains an API key.
